title: With every model
question: Does a wider pool, with 7 flagship and budget models added, pay off?

added.data_policy: OpenRouter paid route pinned to OpenAI (standard tier).
OpenRouter paid route pinned to Google AI Studio (standard tier).
OpenRouter paid route pinned to Moonshot AI (its own MXFP4 deployment).
OpenRouter paid route pinned to OpenAI (standard tier).
OpenRouter paid route pinned to Xiaomi (its own FP8 deployment).
OpenRouter paid route pinned to Meta.
OpenRouter paid route pinned to Mistral (zero data retention).

excluded.reason: Stopped on 2026-11-14 after 375 of 900 prompts. Its reasoning ignored the 4,096-token answer limit on knowledge questions (one answer ran to 35,234 tokens and ten minutes), so finishing would have taken the flagship runs past their $25 budget.

Stopped on 2026-11-21 after 884 of 900 prompts: all 600 suite prompts and 284 of the 300 fresh ones. The runner's free-request ceiling (950 a day, kept under the account's 1,000) was reached, so 16 fresh prompts were never sent; they can run after the daily quota resets.
Smoke-tested on 8 prompts, then not run in full (0 of 900 prompts): the account's 1,000 free requests a day covered one free model on 2026-11-21, and NVIDIA is already in the pool.

router.selection_rule: Lower validation log loss between logistic regression and gradient-boosted trees, as the proposal specifies; the train-to-validation gap is the overfitting check.

protocol: The flagships (GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 4 Carbon, Kimi K3.1 Pro) answered the 600 suite prompts and the 300 fresh prompts on 2026-11-14 through OpenRouter, each pinned to one host (its maker's own where there is one), with the same prompts, token limits, retry policy, and grading as the Checkpoint 3 pool.

The budget models (GPT-6 Luna, MiMo-V2.6 Flash, Muse Ember, Ministral 8B) answered the 600 suite prompts and the 300 fresh prompts on 2026-11-21 through OpenRouter, each pinned to one host (its maker's own where there is one), with the same prompts, token limits, retry policy, and grading as the Checkpoint 3 pool.

Grok 4.7 is left out: Stopped on 2026-11-14 after 375 of 900 prompts. Its reasoning ignored the 4,096-token answer limit on knowledge questions (one answer ran to 35,234 tokens and ten minutes), so finishing would have taken the flagship runs past their $25 budget.

ERNIE 5.5 Flash (free preview) is left out: Stopped on 2026-11-21 after 884 of 900 prompts: all 600 suite prompts and 284 of the 300 fresh ones. The runner's free-request ceiling (950 a day, kept under the account's 1,000) was reached, so 16 fresh prompts were never sent; they can run after the daily quota resets.

Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (free) is left out: Smoke-tested on 8 prompts, then not run in full (0 of 900 prompts): the account's 1,000 free requests a day covered one free model on 2026-11-21, and NVIDIA is already in the pool.

The study's router uses the Checkpoint 3 recipe unchanged on all 16 models: classifier family and regularization chosen on validation log loss, presets tuned on the validation split with the same grids and accuracy floors, then refit on train + validation.
The strongest added model, Gemini 4 Carbon, is the one with the most right answers on the train and validation prompts, fixed before the test and fresh results were read.

The paired comparisons were fixed in code before the added models' results were read; p-values are Holm-adjusted within each evaluation. Intervals are 95% bootstrap intervals over prompts (10,000 resamples, fixed seed).

The fresh prompts were already read twice, for the frozen router and the flagship study. The budget models were chosen from the live catalog by price before any of their results were read, and nothing here was tuned on the fresh prompts.

evaluations.title: Original test split
evaluations.description: The 120 held-out test prompts of the 600-prompt suite, answered by the Checkpoint 3 pool in late October and by the flagships on 2026-11-14 and the budget models on 2026-11-21.

comparisons.question: Does the best-quality setting get more right with the wider pool?
Does the wider pool change the lowest-cost setting?
